briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Weathers the Weed Tax While National Cannabis & Psychedelics Momentum Builds
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis market keeps finding ways around its 24% wholesale tax — new storefronts, a live legal challenge, and a toss-up governor's race that could still bring relief. Nationally, a DEA procedural pause on rescheduling shares the news cycle with real momentum: Trulieve's NYSE debut, a $1.5B Apollo bet on cannabis trade shows, and psilocybin edging toward a historic FDA approval.

local.text: Menominee eyes four more dispensary licenses — A citizen petition drive qualified for the November ballot to raise the city's dispensary cap from nine to 13, opening fresh retail opportunity in the Upper Peninsula.

Henry Ford Health lands $1M cannabis research grant — A researcher there secured federal funding to help pregnant Michiganders cut back on cannabis, adding the state to the list driving clinical science on the plant.

Ann Arbor keeps adding storefronts as brands compete — Michigan-based Lume Cannabis Co. is opening its newest Ann Arbor location at 2247 W. Liberty Street, joining a crowded but still-growing local retail scene.

Tax lawsuit still alive, could force relief — The Michigan Cannabis Industry Association's second legal challenge argues the 24% wholesale tax unconstitutionally exceeds the state's 6% sales-tax cap, keeping relief in play for operators.

Prices stay low, demand steady despite new tax — Oversupply has kept Michigan dispensary prices competitive and sales volume resilient even as the 24% wholesale tax took hold, per Cannabis Business Times.

national.text: DEA pauses rescheduling hearing, doesn't kill it — Chief Judge Derek Julius paused the Schedule III review to weigh a GAO report on scheduling gaps, but the stay sets no end date and leaves April's medical-cannabis reclassification intact.

Trulieve wins approval for NYSE listing — The MSO completed a medical-only restructuring to maintain its Schedule III footprint and will begin trading under ticker TRLV, a milestone for plant-touching operators.

Apollo Global bets $1.5B on cannabis trade shows — The private equity giant is acquiring MJBizCon parent Emerald Holding and trade-show producer Questex, signaling institutional confidence in the sector's infrastructure.
Compass Pathways builds out team for 2027 launch — The psilocybin drugmaker hired a new chief people officer to help guide COMP360 toward a planned first-half 2027 rollout pending FDA approval.

Oregon's psilocybin program shows lasting, safe results — A new OHSU-backed study found low rates of harm and durable benefits among adults using the state's regulated psilocybin services, bolstering the case for broader access.
